news.title: Billions in revenue proves Fifa right on the World Cup – but only on things it cares about
news.lede: The 2026 edition of the tournament brought in untold amounts of money to Gianni Infantino’s governing body. The total hasn’t entirely stopped rising yet, still clicking away towards a final tally. Still, Fifa has already announced that it surpassed its own lofty revenue projections for the 2026 World Cup, bringing in $15bn, significantly more than anticipated. It appears that a third of that total – $5bn – came from ticket sales and hospitality alone, per reporting from the Times.

news.title: Fans get golden chance to buy 2022 World Cup trophy lifted by Lionel Messi
news.lede: The replica World Cup trophy carried by Lionel Messi after Argentina's victory in 2022 will go under the hammer as part of an exclusive auction. The replica will headline the inaugural Sports Memorabilia Auction by Richmond Auctions on 7 November, with one of sport's most iconic pieces up for grabs. The trophy was carried onto the pitch by the legendary Messi after one of the greatest finals ever played, with the Argentinian scoring twice to fire his country to a third global triumph despite Kylian Mbappé netting a hat-trick for France. As the celebrations rolled on long after the final whistle, the replica made its way from the stands into the players’ hands and was passed from champion to champion for 45 minutes during their on-pitch celebrations.

news.title: The World Cup Didn't Change Norway. It Changed How the World Noticed Norway.
news.lede: For years, Norway had a branding challenge that most countries would envy: people liked Norway, they just didn't think about it very often. Then came the 2026 FIFA World Cup. Suddenly, millions of people around the world were talking about Norwegian football, Erling Braut Haaland, Viking “Row” celebrations, salmon, brown cheese and the values Norway represents. The tournament became much more than a sporting event.

news.title: Soccer-Former Brazil captain Cafu says Neymar leaves proud legacy as Ancelotti begins rebuild
news.lede: SAO PAULO, Nov 4 (Reuters) - ⁠Former Brazil captain Cafu said Neymar's international career should be remembered as a successful ⁠and honourable one after the forward retired from the national team following Brazil's disappointing ‌World Cup campaign this year. Neymar, Brazil's all-time leading scorer, said in late July that he no longer wanted to play for the national team, weeks after suggesting his international career had ended following Brazil's last-16 defeat by Norway at the ​World Cup. "The end of the cycle with the national team ⁠comes for everyone," Cafu, Brazil's most-capped player ⁠with 150 appearances, told Reuters on Tuesday. "The most important thing is that his cycle was a ⁠successful ‌one.
